subtype: Approach: following a rule set in advance [Thinking]
passage: “Simran, I'll tell you about the night I was fifteen and a stranger rang. I'm Karthik, your Mama. Years ago, my father sat us all down and made one rule: OTPs, PINs and passwords stay secret from everyone. Not with the bank, not with the police, not with me. We didn't argue about it. That night the caller was polite. He knew my name and my father's, and said the account was in danger. I said, ‘Sir, family rule. I can't give any code.’ His voice hardened. He said I would be sorry. I put the phone down and my heart was pounding, but I didn't have to decide anything, because it was already decided.”

qa.a: OTPs, PINs and passwords stay secret from everyone.

qa.q: How did Karthik feel when the caller's voice hardened?
qa.a: Shaky, with a pounding heart, but steady: he did not have to argue because the answer was already decided.

qa.q: Which choice in the story kept Karthik safe, and why?
qa.a: Following the family rule without debating it, because a convincing voice cannot talk someone out of an answer already agreed.

qa.q: How might Karthik's father have felt when he heard about the call?
qa.a: He was probably relieved and proud that the rule had worked, and glad it had been agreed at the family table beforehand.

grounding: An elder recalls a family rule set in advance that lets a teen refuse a convincing caller without debating.

subtype: Approach: following a rule set in advance [Thinking]
passage:
The sangeet music was so loud that Seema had to press the phone to one ear and cover the other. The caller sounded kind and tired, like a real office worker. “Beta, your uncle Vishal's courier is stuck with us. He gave your number as backup. I'm sending an OTP just to confirm delivery. Tell me the six digits and it's done.”
Vishal Mama was dancing in the next room, too far to ask over the noise. The man knew his full name. He sounded so reasonable.
But Seema didn't start weighing it up. At home they had decided it at the dinner table last Diwali: OTPs, PINs and passwords never go to anyone, whatever the story. I don't have to decide if he's honest, she thought. The rule already decided.
“Sorry, we don't share OTPs,” she said, and cut the call.
Later, over the noise, Vishal Mama said he hadn't ordered anything at all.

qa.q: When had Seema's family agreed on the rule?
qa.a: At the dinner table last Diwali.

qa.q: Why didn't Seema try to judge whether the caller was honest?
qa.a: She felt steadier leaning on the rule; it had already decided, so the kind voice and the loud room couldn't pull her into doubt.

qa.q: What else could Seema do after cutting the call?
qa.a: Tell Vishal Mama and her parents once the music stops, so the family knows someone is using his name.

qa.q: How might Vishal Mama see the call when he hears about it?
qa.a: He would likely be startled that someone used his name, and glad the family rule held while he was out of reach.

grounding: Shows a teen applying a family rule never to share OTPs without debating it, which holds even when the caller sounds kind and convincing.

subtype: Approach: following a rule set in advance [Thinking]
passage:
The call came while Tarun was helping Hansa Ba set up her new phone in their Ahmedabad flat. The caller said he was from Tarun's school office, knew the class teacher's name, and apologised warmly for the trouble. “The parent portal has a glitch. Just read me the password so we can fix your fee record before tomorrow.”
Hansa Ba looked up. “Is it the school?”
It sounded like the school. For a moment Tarun felt the pull to be helpful. Then he heard Papa's voice from the family meeting in the summer: passwords, PINs and OTPs don't go to anyone, for any reason. If the rule has no exceptions, he thought, I don't need to work out who's calling.
“I don't share passwords. My father will call the school,” he said, and hung up.
Papa phoned the office that evening. There was no glitch.

qa.q: What did the caller ask Tarun to read out?
qa.a: The password for the parent portal.

qa.q: What was Tarun feeling when the call sounded like the school?
qa.a: Tarun felt a pull to be helpful and a moment of doubt, then relief that the family rule left nothing to decide.

qa.q: How could Tarun use this call to help Hansa Ba with her new phone?
qa.a: Teach her the same rule right then, since she has just heard a convincing caller and may get similar calls.

qa.q: What might Hansa Ba make of what she saw?
qa.a: Hansa Ba might be impressed that a fixed rule beat a caller who sounded so real, and reassured about her own safety.

grounding: Shows a teen applying a family rule never to share passwords, PINs or OTPs, which works even when the caller knows details and sounds genuine.
